sections.title: Fact first, comment after
sections.content: You know *molestar* from A2 Unit 27: a feeling about something takes the subjunctive. Sometimes you want to start the sentence with the fact itself and comment on it afterwards. Spanish uses *el hecho de que* ('the fact that'): *El hecho de que llegue tarde me molesta*. Both people already know the fact, so you are not announcing it, you are commenting on it. That is why the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive.

sections.title: El hecho de que + subjunctive
rows: El hecho de que llegue tarde me molesta.
The fact that he arrives late bothers me.
El hecho de que hayan ganado no es una excusa.
The fact that they have won is not an excuse.
El hecho de que lloviera no cambió nuestros planes.
The fact that it rained did not change our plans.
Me molesta el hecho de que llegue tarde.
I am bothered by the fact that he arrives late.

sections.title: Agreement and tense
sections.content: The comment agrees with *el hecho*, which is singular: *El hecho de que lleguen tarde me molesta*, not *me molestan*. You can also deny a consequence: *El hecho de que sea tarde no significa que no puedas llamar*. After a past verb you use the imperfect subjunctive, as in *Quería que vinieras* from B1 Unit 38: *llegara*, *lloviera*.

items.spanish: El hecho de que el tren llegue con retraso me molesta.
items.english: The fact that the train arrives late bothers me.

items.spanish: El hecho de que ella llegue tarde no la disculpa.
items.english: The fact that she arrives late does not excuse her.

items.spanish: El hecho de que hayan ganado no significa que tengan razón.
items.english: The fact that they have won does not mean that they are right.

items.spanish: El hecho de que lloviera no cambió nuestros planes.
items.english: The fact that it rained did not change our plans.

sections.content: Always write *el hecho de que*, with *de*: *el hecho que* is a common mistake. You may sometimes read the indicative after it, when the writer wants to stress that the fact is true. At B2, use the subjunctive when you are commenting on a fact.
